category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: In the context of transmission-based precautions, pathogens larger than 5 µm that travel short distances (3–6 feet) through coughing or sneezing require the implementation of [___] precautions.
back:
Droplet Precautions.
• Requires a surgical mask for healthcare staff.
• Private room preferred; the door may remain open.
• Targets agents like Influenza, Pertussis, and Neisseria meningitidis.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient is admitted with a draining wound infected with Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Describe the PPE and room requirements needed to prevent cross-contamination according to UHS board protocols.
back:
Contact Precautions.
• Mandatory gown and gloves for all patient/environment contact.
• Dedicated patient equipment (e.g., stethoscope, thermometer).
• Strict hand hygiene and use of liquid soap for spore-forming agents like C. difficile.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain the mechanism by which Airborne Infection Isolation Rooms (AIIR) utilize pressure gradients to prevent the spread of infectious droplet nuclei.
back:
• Negative Pressure Gradient: Air flows into the room from corridors, preventing escape of suspended nuclei (<5 µm).
• Ventilation: Minimum 6–12 air changes per hour.
• Filtration: Exhausted air is passed through HEPA filters or vented directly outdoors.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: To achieve complete sterilization of surgical instruments, the autoclave must be operated at [___]°C for 15 minutes at 15 lb/in² pressure.
back:
• 121°C
• Ensures destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores like Clostridium.
• Utilizes moist heat, which is more effective than dry heat at lower temperatures.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A pediatric patient is admitted with a generalized vesicular rash. To prevent nosocomial spread, identify the appropriate isolation protocol and duration.
back:
• Strict isolation (Airborne and Contact precautions).
• Maintain until all lesions have crusted.
• Critical for protecting immunocompromised patients from Varicella-Zoster transmission.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the role of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist in preventing the transmission of infection and improving patient outcomes.
back:
• Standardizes communication at induction, incision, and before leaving the OR.
• Verifies antibiotic prophylaxis administration within 60 minutes before incision.
• Confirms sterility indicators and equipment issues through multidisciplinary teamwork.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 30-year-old male was exposed to a patient with active Meningococcal meningitis. Distinguish between 'Isolation' and 'Quarantine' protocols for this scenario.
back:
• Isolation: Separates the *infected* person during the period of communicability.
• Quarantine: Restricts the *healthy contact* for the duration of the longest incubation period.
• Both aim to break the chain of transmission.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the core components of Standard Precautions used for all patients to prevent the spread of infectious agents.
back:
• Hand hygiene before and after every patient contact.
• Use of PPE (gloves, gowns, masks) based on anticipated exposure.
• Safe handling/disposal of sharps and respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The most effective skin antiseptic used in medical practice for preparation before obtaining blood cultures or installing central catheters is [___].
back:
• Iodine-containing compounds (e.g., Tincture of Iodine or Iodophors).
• Superior to 70% ethanol for reducing skin flora contamination.
• Iodophors are preferred for surgery as they are less irritating.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 70-year-old patient on a ventilator is at risk for nosocomial infection. Which bundle of care practices is most effective for preventing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP)?
back:
• Elevating the head of the bed to 30-45 degrees.
• Daily sedation holidays and assessment for extubation.
• Meticulous hand hygiene and oral decontamination with chlorhexidine.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Discuss the epidemiological strategy of 'breaking the weakest link' in the chain of infection transmission.
back:
• Targets the most vulnerable point: reservoir, route, or susceptible host.
• Route interruption includes water chlorination and food sanitation.
• Host protection includes active immunization and chemoprophylaxis.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the clinical application of 'Disinfectants' with 'Antiseptics' in a hospital setting.
back:
• Disinfectants: Strong chemicals (e.g., bleach) used only on inanimate objects (fomites).
• Antiseptics: Less toxic chemicals (e.g., Chlorhexidine) safe for living tissue/skin.
• Disinfectants are often too caustic for biological surfaces.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: State the clinical significance of statutory 'Notification' of infectious diseases to health authorities.
back:
• Permits early detection of outbreaks and immediate control measures.
• Provides essential data for national epidemiological surveillance.
• Mandatory for diseases considered serious public health threats (e.g., Cholera).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Airborne precautions are indicated for pathogens smaller than [___] microns that remain suspended in air and travel long distances.
back:
5 microns.
- Pathogens like TB remain suspended longer than larger droplets.
- Requires N95 respirators and negative pressure rooms.
- Differs from droplet precautions (>5 microns).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A 22-year-old male presents with sudden high fever, nuchal rigidity, and a petechial rash. Identify the specific isolation protocol required for this patient.
back:
Droplet Precautions.
- Used for Neisseria meningitidis.
- Wear a surgical mask when within 3–6 feet.
- Maintain a private room or cohort patients with the same infection.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain how an Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) functions to prevent the spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to healthcare corridors.
back:
Maintains negative air pressure.
- Air flows from hallways into the room (inward).
- Exhausted air passes through HEPA filters.
- Requires 6–12 air changes per hour.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the respiratory protection requirements for a physician treating a patient with Seasonal Influenza versus one with Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
back:
Influenza (Droplet): Surgical mask is sufficient.
- TB (Airborne): Fit-tested N95 or higher respirator required.
- Influenza droplets fall rapidly; TB nuclei remain suspended indefinitely.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Specify the required modification to hand hygiene protocols when exiting a room designated for Contact Precautions due to Clostridioides difficile.
back:
Use soap and water only.
- Alcohol-based rubs do not kill C. diff spores.
- Physical friction/rinsing is necessary to mechanically remove spores.
- Gloves must be removed before washing.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: The minimum Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) required for staff before entering a room designated for Contact Precautions consists of [___].
back:
Gown and Gloves.
- Donned upon entry; removed before exit.
- Prevents contamination of skin and clothing.
- Indicated for MRSA, VRE, and major wound infections.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient is admitted with a disseminated vesicular rash suspected to be Varicella (chickenpox). Which combination of precaution protocols must be implemented?
back:
Airborne + Contact Precautions.
- Airborne for respiratory aerosols.
- Contact for direct fluid from lesions.
- Requires N95 respirator, gown, and gloves.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Describe the physical dynamics of 'Droplet' transmission that limit the necessary isolation distance to approximately 3–6 feet from the source.
back:
Gravity-dependent large particles.
- Droplets (>5μm) are too heavy to stay airborne.
- They fall quickly onto environmental surfaces.
- Transmission requires close mucosal contact.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish the masking requirements for a patient being transported to Radiology under Droplet versus Airborne precautions.
back:
Both require the patient to wear a surgical mask.
- Mask filters exhaled large droplets and aerosols at source.
- Patients do not wear N95 masks.
- Notify receiving department in advance.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Identify the clinical circumstances and patient population for which 'Standard Precautions' should be applied by healthcare workers.
back:
All patients at all times.
- Applied to blood, body fluids, and non-intact skin.
- Assumes every patient is potentially infectious.
- Includes hand hygiene and appropriate barrier use.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Infection prevention for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) requires the use of [___] precautions.
back: Contact Precautions. • Used for MDROs and enteric infections. • Requires gown and gloves for all patient interactions. • Dedicated patient-care equipment is mandatory to prevent cross-contamination.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient presents with persistent cough, night sweats, and weight loss. Sputum smear is positive for Acid-Fast Bacilli. State the specific room requirements for this patient.
back: Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR). • Requires negative pressure ventilation. • Minimum of 6 to 12 air changes per hour. • Exhausted air must be HEPA-filtered or vented directly outdoors.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain how droplet transmission differs from airborne transmission regarding particle size and environmental behavior.
back: Particle Dynamics. • Droplets: Large (>5 microns), travel short distances (~3-6 feet), and settle quickly. • Airborne: Small nuclei (<5 microns), remain suspended in air, and travel long distances.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the respiratory protection required for a healthcare worker entering a room of a patient with Pertussis versus a patient with pulmonary Tuberculosis.
back: Respiratory PPE Comparison. • Pertussis: Requires a standard surgical mask (Droplet Precautions). • Tuberculosis: Requires a fit-tested N95 respirator or higher (Airborne Precautions).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Specify the necessary Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for a healthcare worker entering a room under Contact Precautions.
back: Contact PPE Requirements. • Clean non-sterile gloves are mandatory. • Isolation gown required for all interactions. • Donning must occur before room entry; doffing must occur before exit.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Patients suspected of having Neisseria meningitidis infection must be placed on [___] precautions until 24 hours of effective antibiotic therapy.
back: Droplet Precautions. • Surgical mask for staff within 3-6 feet of patient. • Patient must wear a mask during transport. • Private room is preferred for isolation.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A 2-year-old is admitted with a maculopapular rash and fever. Varicella (Chickenpox) is suspected. Identify the two types of transmission-based precautions required.
back: Airborne and Contact Precautions. • N95 respirator required for staff entry. • Gown and gloves required for skin/lesion contact. • Precautions continue until all lesions have completely crusted.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Detail the protocol for hand hygiene when managing a patient with Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) under contact precautions.
back: C. difficile Hand Hygiene. • Use soap and water specifically for handwashing. • Alcohol-based rubs are ineffective against C. diff spores. • Friction during washing is essential for mechanical removal.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Differentiate the environmental controls needed for Droplet vs. Airborne precautions.
back: Environmental Controls. • Droplet: No special ventilation; 3-foot spatial separation is baseline. • Airborne: Negative pressure (AIIR); air filtered or vented outside. • Droplet allows standard rooms.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Name the three major categories of transmission-based precautions used in addition to Standard Precautions.
back: Transmission-Based Precaution Categories. • Contact Precautions for direct/indirect contact. • Droplet Precautions for large respiratory particles. • Airborne Precautions for aerosolized micro-particles.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: To prevent the inhalation of small droplet nuclei (<5 μm) in a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis, the healthcare worker must wear an [___] respirator.
back: * N95 Respirator. * Filters 95% of airborne particles. * Requires specific fit-testing. * Essential for airborne precautions.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A 19-year-old student presents with high fever, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash. While awaiting confirmation of Neisseria meningitidis, the appropriate infection control category is [___] precautions.
back: * Droplet Precautions. * Targets large respiratory particles (>5 μm). * Required for pathogens traveling 3-6 feet. * PPE includes a standard surgical mask.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain the biological basis for using standard surgical masks in droplet precautions versus respirators in airborne precautions.
back: * Droplets (>5 μm) fall quickly via gravity. * Surgical masks provide a physical fluid barrier. * Airborne nuclei (<5 μm) remain suspended in air. * Respirators provide high-efficiency particulate filtration.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the room placement and ventilation requirements for a patient with Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) versus Varicella.
back: * MRSA: Private room (Contact); standard ventilation. * Varicella: Negative-pressure room (Airborne). * Varicella requires 6-12 air exchanges/hour. * Varicella needs HEPA filtration or external exhaust.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Specify the personal protective equipment (PPE) required for entering the room of a patient with Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE) and the correct sequence.
back: * PPE: Gown and gloves. * Hand hygiene must precede donning. * PPE must be donned upon entry. * PPE must be removed before exiting.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Droplet precautions are generally indicated for pathogens that do not travel more than [___] feet from the source.
back: * 3 to 6 feet. * Large particles settle rapidly due to mass. * Mask required within this specific radius. * Spatial separation of beds is required.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient with a history of productive cough and night sweats has acid-fast bacilli in their sputum. Detail the specific room engineering required for this patient.
back: * Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR). * Negative air pressure relative to corridors. * Monitored pressure differential. * Air exhausted directly outside or HEPA filtered.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain why hand hygiene with soap and water is specifically mandated over alcohol-based rubs when exiting a room of a patient with Clostridioides difficile.
back: * C. difficile produces hardy endospores. * Alcohol-based sanitizers lack sporicidal activity. * Soap and water provide mechanical removal. * Essential for breaking the contact chain.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish between the primary mode of transmission for Influenza and Measles to determine the necessary isolation precaution.
back: * Influenza: Droplet; standard surgical mask. * Measles: Airborne; N95 and negative pressure. * Influenza particles settle; Measles nuclei stay suspended. * Influenza requires 3-6 feet separation.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Identify the transmission route for Norovirus and the specific precaution type required in a hospital setting.
back: * Route: Fecal-oral (Direct/Indirect contact). * Precaution: Contact precautions. * Requires gloves and gown for entry. * High environmental stability necessitates thorough disinfection.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: For pathogens transmitted via micro-particles that remain suspended in air currents for long durations, healthcare providers must utilize a(n) [___] as the minimum respiratory protection.
back:
• N95 Respirator
• Provides high-efficiency filtration of particles <5 microns
• Requires annual fit-testing to ensure a tight facial seal
• Used for Airborne Precautions.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient is admitted with a large sacral pressure ulcer colonized with Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE). Identify the mandatory transmission-based precaution category and its required barriers.
back:
• Contact Precautions
• Gown and gloves required for all patient/environment contact
• Dedicated patient-care equipment (e.g., stethoscope)
• Prioritize private room or cohorting with similar MDRO patients.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain how the physical size of infectious particles determines the distance of transmission in Droplet versus Airborne precautions.
back:
• Droplets: >5 microns; heavy particles that settle within 3-6 feet of the source.
• Airborne: ≤5 microns; evaporate into 'droplet nuclei' that travel long distances via air currents.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the environmental engineering controls required for a patient with Neisseria meningitidis versus a patient with suspected Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
back:
• Meningitis (Droplet): Standard ventilation; private room preferred (door can be open).
• Tuberculosis (Airborne): AIIR (Airborne Infection Isolation Room); negative pressure, 6-12 air changes/hour, exhaust vented outdoors.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Identify the mandatory chemical hand hygiene step required when exiting a room of a patient under contact precautions for Clostridioides difficile.
back:
• Soap and Water washing
• Hand rubbing with soap physically removes alcohol-resistant spores
• Alcohol-based rubs are ineffective against C. difficile spores.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: To prevent transmission of the Influenza virus from a symptomatic patient, the clinician should don a(n) [___] upon entry as part of Droplet Precautions.
back:
• Surgical Mask
• Protects mucous membranes from large respiratory droplets
• Discarded after each encounter; combined with eye protection if splashing is anticipated.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A 4-year-old child presents with a maculopapular rash starting on the face and Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa. Determine the precaution protocol necessary for hospital admission.
back:
• Airborne Precautions
• Indicated for Measles (Rubeola)
• Negative pressure room required
• Only immune staff should attend; N95 respirator mandatory for all.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Describe the mechanism by which 'Standard Precautions' differ from 'Transmission-Based Precautions' in the hospital setting.
back:
• Standard: Applied to all patients regardless of diagnosis (blood, body fluids, non-intact skin).
• Transmission-Based: Supplemental precautions (Contact/Droplet/Airborne) tailored to specific known or suspected infectious agents.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish between the physiological route of entry for pathogens requiring Droplet precautions versus those requiring Contact precautions.
back:
• Droplet: Pathogen enters via mucous membranes (nose, mouth, conjunctiva) from respiratory secretions.
• Contact: Pathogen enters via direct contact or contaminated fomites (skin, wounds, gastrointestinal tract).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Specify the primary structural requirement for a healthcare worker's facial PPE to be classified as an N95 respirator.
back:
• Tight-fitting facial seal
• Must filter ≥95% of 0.3-micron airborne particles
• Unlike loose-fitting surgical masks, it prevents air leakage around the edges.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: For patients with suspected Mycobacterium tuberculosis, healthcare workers must utilize [___] precautions, including the use of a fit-tested N95 respirator.
back:
• Airborne Precautions
• Prevents transmission of small infectious particles (<5 µm)
• Particles stay suspended in air for extended periods

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
coreConcept: Contact Plus Precautions for Spore-Forming Organisms
front: A patient is admitted with profuse watery diarrhea and a positive stool toxin assay for Clostridium difficile. Identify the specific isolation precautions and mandatory hand hygiene practice required.
back:
• Contact Precautions
• Mandatory hand hygiene with soap and water (friction removes spores)
• Alcohol-based gels are ineffective against C. difficile spores

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain the role of particle size and gravity in the transmission mechanism of pathogens requiring droplet precautions.
back:
• Large droplets (>5 µm) generated via coughing or sneezing
• Heavy particles travel short distances (usually <3-6 feet)
• Transmission occurs through mucosal contact rather than inhalation into deep alveoli

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the room ventilation requirements and personal protective equipment (PPE) for a patient with Neisseria meningitidis versus one with disseminated Varicella zoster.
back:
• N. meningitidis (Droplet): Standard room; surgical mask for proximity
• Varicella (Airborne + Contact): Negative pressure room (AIIR); N95 respirator plus gown and gloves

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: State the essential structural requirements for an Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) used to manage pulmonary tuberculosis.
back:
• Negative pressure relative to surrounding hallways
• Minimum 6 to 12 air changes per hour
• HEPA filtration of exhausted air or direct external venting

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: In the management of Bordetella pertussis or Influenza virus, the primary PPE required when working within 3 to 6 feet of the patient is a [___].
back:
• Surgical Mask
• Standard masks provide a barrier against large-particle droplets
• Required under Droplet Precautions protocols

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A child presents with high fever, cough, and a maculopapular rash starting at the hairline. Determine the appropriate isolation strategy while awaiting laboratory confirmation for Measles.
back:
• Immediate Airborne Precautions
• Patient placement in a negative pressure room
• Restrict entry to immune staff; others must wear N95 respirators

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Describe the physiological objective of utilizing a 'Positive Pressure' room versus the 'Negative Pressure' room used in standard airborne isolation.
back:
• Positive Pressure: Protects immunocompromised patients from environmental pathogens
• Negative Pressure: Protects the hospital environment from infectious patients (e.g., TB)
• Air flows 'out' of positive rooms and 'into' negative rooms

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish between Standard Precautions and Contact Precautions regarding the mandatory application of gloves and gowns.
back:
• Standard: PPE applied only if contact with blood/body fluids is anticipated
• Contact: Gown and gloves mandatory for every entry into the room
• Both require hand hygiene before and after contact

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Which category of precautions is indicated for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) such as MRSA or VRE found in a surgical wound?
back:
• Contact Precautions
• Requires dedicated patient-care equipment (e.g., stethoscopes)
• Focuses on preventing transmission via hands or contaminated surfaces

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: To prevent the transmission of infectious agents via large respiratory particles (>5 microns) that settle quickly, clinicians must apply [___] precautions.
back: • Droplet precautions • Requires a surgical mask for entry • Targets particles >5 microns • Used for pathogens like Influenza and Pertussis.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient presents with a chronic cough and acid-fast bacilli in the sputum. Identify the mandatory room air-flow requirement for this admission.
back: • Negative pressure ventilation • 6 to 12 air changes per hour • Exhaust air through HEPA filters • Mandatory for Airborne precautions (Tuberculosis).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: How does the barrier function of a standard surgical mask differ from an N95 respirator during infection control?
back: • Surgical mask: Blocks large droplets (>5 microns); loose fit • N95: Filters small nuclei (<5 microns); tight seal • Surgical for Droplet; N95 for Airborne.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish the personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements for a patient with Norovirus versus a patient with Hemophilus influenzae type b.
back: • Norovirus (Contact): Gowns and gloves mandatory • H. influenzae (Droplet): Surgical mask mandatory • Hand hygiene required for both scenarios.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Identify the essential step regarding hand hygiene when exiting a room labeled for Contact Precautions.
back: • Perform hygiene immediately after PPE removal • Use alcohol rub or soap and water • Avoid touching surfaces after hygiene • Prevents environmental cross-contamination.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Infection transmission involving droplet nuclei measuring [___] microns or less requires a negative pressure environment and N95 respirators.
back: • 5 • Defines Airborne precautions • Particles stay suspended in air for long periods • Examples: Measles, Varicella, and Tuberculosis.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A nurse prepares to examine a patient with high fever, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash. Which specific PPE is required for this case?
back: • Surgical mask (Droplet precautions) • Required for suspected Neisseria meningitidis • Wear within 3-6 feet of the patient • Eye protection if splashing expected.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain the mechanism by which negative pressure prevents the spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in a hospital ward.
back: • Air pressure in room is lower than hallway • Creates inward-only airflow at door • Prevents infectious nuclei from entering common corridors • Protects surrounding staff and patients.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Contrast the infective particle buoyancy and travel distance between Droplet and Airborne precautions.
back: • Droplet: Heavy, settle within 3-6 feet, short-term suspension • Airborne: Light, travel long distances, stay suspended indefinitely • Airborne requires environmental ventilation controls.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Which common hand hygiene agent is ineffective against pathogens requiring Contact-Enteric precautions, such as Clostridioides difficile?
back: • Alcohol-based hand rubs • Alcohol fails to kill bacterial spores • Requires mechanical removal with soap and water • Dedicated equipment is also necessary.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: The specific engineering control required for airborne precautions to prevent the outward migration of infectious particles is a [___] pressure room.
back: * Negative pressure room. * Ensures air flows into the room from the corridor. * Requires 6 to 12 air changes per hour. * Exhaust air is HEPA-filtered before release.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A 25-year-old male is admitted with a high-grade fever, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash. For the suspected pathogen, the most appropriate isolation precaution to implement is [___].
back: * Droplet precautions. * Wear a surgical mask when within 3 to 6 feet of the patient. * Pathogen: Neisseria meningitidis. * Maintain for 24 hours post-antibiotic therapy.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain how particle size in microns determines the selection between surgical masks and N95 respirators.
back: * Droplets (>5 microns) are heavy and travel short distances, requiring surgical masks. * Airborne nuclei (<5 microns) remain suspended in air currents for hours, requiring N95 respirators.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient presents with disseminated Varicella-zoster. Contrast the isolation requirements for this case with those for localized MRSA wound infection.
back: * Varicella: Airborne and Contact precautions (N95, negative pressure, gown, and gloves). * MRSA: Contact precautions only (Gown and gloves for patient or environmental contact).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Identify the mandatory hand hygiene modification required when managing a patient under contact precautions for Clostridioides difficile.
back: * Hand washing with soap and water is required. * Alcohol-based rubs are ineffective against spores. * Physical friction and rinsing are necessary to mechanically remove the spores.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: For effective airborne isolation, the healthcare provider must utilize a fit-tested [___] respirator to filter 95% of particles as small as 0.3 microns.
back: * N95 respirator. * Essential for TB, Measles, and Varicella. * Provides a tight facial seal compared to surgical masks. * Prevents inhalation of droplet nuclei.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is hospitalized. Outline the primary engineering control and PPE required for staff prior to room entry.
back: * Engineering: Negative Pressure Isolation Room (AIIR). * PPE: N95 respirator must be donned before entry. * Prevents transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis nuclei suspended in air.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain the biological basis for requiring N95 respirators for measles but only surgical masks for pertussis.
back: * Measles (airborne) uses tiny droplet nuclei that stay buoyant and bypass surgical mask gaps. * Pertussis (droplet) involves larger particles that settle quickly, making surgical masks sufficient.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish between the isolation protocols for Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE).
back: * Mycoplasma: Droplet precautions (Surgical mask). * VRE: Contact precautions (Gown and gloves). * Both require dedicated patient equipment and strict hand hygiene to prevent horizontal spread.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: List the mandatory components of Standard Precautions used for every patient regardless of suspected infection status.
back: * Hand hygiene before/after contact. * PPE based on anticipated fluid exposure. * Safe injection practices. * Proper handling of contaminated sharps/linen and respiratory hygiene.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Isolation precautions for large respiratory particles that do not remain suspended in the air are classified as [___] precautions.
back: Droplet Precautions; Particles >5 micrometers in size; Travel distance usually less than 6 feet.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A patient is admitted with a large, draining wound positive for Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Identify the primary isolation precaution indicated.
back: Contact Precautions; Wear gown and gloves for all interactions; Use dedicated patient equipment like stethoscopes.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain why alcohol-based hand rubs are ineffective against Clostridioides difficile, necessitating the use of contact precautions with soap and water.
back: C. difficile produces resilient spores; Alcohol does not penetrate spore coats; Mechanical washing is required to remove spores.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Distinguish between 'Standard Precautions' and 'Transmission-Based Precautions' in infection control.
back: Standard: Applied to all patients regardless of diagnosis; Transmission-Based: Added for specific routes (Contact, Droplet, Airborne).

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Name the specific isolation category required for a patient presenting with suspected Neisseria meningitidis infection.
back: Droplet Precautions; Wear surgical mask within 6 feet; Maintain for 24 hours of effective antibiotic therapy.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: In patients with active pulmonary Tuberculosis, the use of a(n) [___] respirator is mandatory for all healthcare personnel entering the room.
back: N95 (or higher) respirator; Filters 95 percent of small airborne particles; Requires annual fit-testing.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: A pediatric patient presents with a 'slapped-cheek' rash and fever. Determine the appropriate isolation precautions if the patient is immunocompromised.
back: Droplet precautions; Targeted at Parvovirus B19; Standard precautions are typically sufficient for immunocompetent hosts.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Explain how the 'negative pressure' mechanism prevents the transmission of airborne pathogens to other hospital areas.
back: Maintains lower pressure in room than hallway; Air flows into room when doors open; Exhausted air is HEPA-filtered.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: Differentiate the air handling requirements for a patient on droplet precautions compared to airborne precautions.
back: Droplet: Standard ventilation and open door permitted; Airborne: Negative pressure and door must remain closed.

category: Differentiate between contact, droplet, and airborne precautions for infection prevention and control
front: State the minimum distance (in feet) recommended between a patient on droplet precautions and other patients in a multi-bed ward.
back: 3 to 6 feet; Prevents direct droplet spray transmission; Physical barriers like curtains are recommended.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The removal of all forms of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial spores, is termed [___].
back:
• Sterilization
• Achieved via autoclaving (121°C at 15 psi for 15-20 minutes)
• Ethylene oxide used for heat-sensitive instruments
• Filtration preferred for intravenous solutions

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A patient with pulmonary tuberculosis has just begun effective chemotherapy. Determine the required duration for physical isolation to prevent droplet spread.
back:
• Typically 3 weeks of effective chemotherapy
• Focuses on rendering the patient non-infectious
• Replaces older long-term physical isolation models
• Chemical isolation is achieved via rapid treatment

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the role of 70% ethanol as an antiseptic during skin preparation for venipuncture.
back:
• Disorganizes lipid structures in cell membranes
• Denatures bacterial proteins
• Requires water for maximal efficacy (70% is superior to 100%)
• Cleans skin but is less effective than iodine

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the application and objective of 'Isolation' versus 'Quarantine' in disease control.
back:
• Isolation: Separates infected persons for the period of communicability
• Quarantine: Limits movement of healthy contacts exposed to infection
• Quarantine duration: Equals the longest usual incubation period

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: List the three mandatory time points for performing the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist to prevent operative errors.
back:
• Before induction of anaesthesia (Sign In)
• Before skin incision (Time Out)
• Before the patient leaves the operating room (Sign Out)

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Standard precautions to prevent healthcare-associated infections mandate the use of [___] whenever contact with blood or body fluids is anticipated.
back:
• Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
• Includes gloves, gowns, masks, and eye protection
• Applied to all patients regardless of suspected infection
• Hand hygiene remains the primary defensive measure

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 6-year-old child presents with a vesicular rash diagnosed as Chickenpox. Identify the specific clinical milestone that marks the end of the required isolation period.
back:
• Until all lesions have crusted over
• Usually takes approximately 6 days after rash onset
• Prevents transmission to susceptible school or home contacts

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the biological function of the 'Ring Immunization' strategy in controlling outbreaks.
back:
• Encircles infected individuals with a barrier of immune persons
• Pathogen cannot find susceptible hosts to continue spreading
• Historically used for the global eradication of smallpox

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish the 'Person Approach' from the 'System Approach' regarding medical error analysis.
back:
• Person Approach: Blames individuals for errors of execution/omission
• System Approach: Examines why systems failed rather than who erred
• System focus: Robustness, resilience, and latent conditions (Swiss Cheese Model)

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the primary route of pathogen spread in hospital wards that is most effectively interrupted by thorough hand hygiene.
back:
• Direct contact via the hands of healthcare staff
• Can transfer microbes between patients or from environment
• Single most critical measure to prevent cross-infection

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The standard process for sterilization of surgical instruments involving exposure to steam at 121°C under 15 lb/in² pressure for 15 minutes is known as [___].
back:
• Autoclaving.
• Kills all microorganisms including resistant bacterial spores.
• Denatures proteins through moist heat.
• Preferred method for heat-stable medical equipment.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A post-operative patient is diagnosed with a wound infection caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Identify the specific transmission-based isolation category required.
back:
• Contact Precautions.
• Requires a private room or cohorting with similar cases.
• Healthcare workers must wear gloves and gowns upon entry.
• Dedicated patient-care equipment must be used.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the biological mechanism that makes 70% ethanol a more effective skin antiseptic than 100% ethanol.
back:
• Water is required for maximal protein denaturation.
• 100% alcohol causes rapid surface protein coagulation, creating a barrier.
• 70% concentration allows better penetration into the microbial cell and membrane disruption.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the respiratory protection and room requirements for a patient with Neisseria meningitidis versus one with suspected Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
back:
• Meningitis: Droplet Precautions; surgical mask required; standard room.
• Tuberculosis: Airborne Precautions; N95/FFP2 respirator required; Negative Pressure Room.
• Airborne particles stay suspended; droplets fall within short distances.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the three specific time points for obligatory checks established by the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist to prevent errors.
back:
• Sign In: Before induction of anaesthesia.
• Time Out: Before skin incision.
• Sign Out: Before the patient leaves the operating room.
• Aims to ensure correct patient, site, and procedure.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: For heat-sensitive items like endoscopes and respiratory therapy equipment, the most effective liquid chemical sterilant used is [___].
back:
• Glutaraldehyde.
• Ten times more effective than formaldehyde and less toxic.
• Acts by alkylating amino and hydroxyl groups of proteins/nucleic acids.
• Provides high-level disinfection/sterilization.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A healthcare worker suffers a needle-stick injury while treating a patient with chronic Hepatitis B. Specify the immediate prevention principle that addresses this 'coal-face' error.
back:
• Standard Precautions.
• Use of 'no-touch' techniques for sharps.
• Immediate use of personal protective equipment (gloves).
• Proper disposal in puncture-proof sharps containers.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Describe the 'Swiss Cheese' model of causation in the context of hospital-acquired infections (HAIs).
back:
• System defences are slices of cheese with holes (weaknesses).
• Errors occur when holes in all layers align.
• Prevents HAIs by adding multiple redundant layers of responsibility and protocols.
• Focuses on system failures over individual blame.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish between the clinical application and safety of antiseptics versus disinfectants.
back:
• Antiseptics: Low toxicity; safe for living tissue/skin (e.g., Ethanol, Iodine).
• Disinfectants: Caustic; used only on inanimate objects (e.g., Phenol, Chlorine).
• Both aim to reduce microbial load to safe levels.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: List the fundamental strategies included in Standard Precautions to protect against blood-borne pathogens.
back:
• Hand hygiene before/after patient contact.
• Use of PPE (gloves, gown, mask) based on risk.
• Safe injection practices and sharps management.
• Proper environmental cleaning and waste disposal.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: In hospital settings, standard autoclave sterilization requires saturated steam at [___] °C under 15 lb/in² pressure for 15-20 minutes to ensure the destruction of bacterial spores.
back:
121

*   Essential for killing heat-resistant spores (e.g., Clostridium).
*   Pressure allows steam to reach temperatures above boiling.
*   Used for surgical instruments and non-heat-sensitive items.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A patient presents with a cough and night sweats. If pulmonary tuberculosis is suspected, the most critical isolation practice to prevent the spread of droplet nuclei is [___].
back:
Respiratory/Airborne Isolation

*   Use of negative pressure rooms.
*   Mandatory N95 respirators for staff.
*   Patient must wear a surgical mask during transport.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain why 70% ethanol is a more effective antiseptic than 100% ethanol for clinical skin preparation.
back:
Requirement of Water

*   Water is necessary for the denaturation of proteins.
*   100% alcohol causes rapid surface coagulation, protecting deeper bacterial structures.
*   70% solution penetrates cell membranes more effectively.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish between the application of 'Quarantine' and 'Isolation' during an outbreak of a communicable disease.
back:
Patient Status Differentiation

*   Quarantine: Restricts movement of healthy people exposed to infection during the incubation period.
*   Isolation: Separates confirmed infected individuals from the healthy population to prevent transmission.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the chemical agent of choice for skin preparation prior to obtaining blood cultures to minimize contamination by Staphylococcus epidermidis.
back:
Iodine or Iodophors (e.g., Povidone-iodine)

*   Provides superior skin antisepsis compared to alcohol alone.
*   Acts as an oxidizing agent.
*   Must be allowed to dry for maximal efficacy.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist requires verbal confirmation of patient identity, site, and procedure at three specific phases: before induction, before incision, and [___].
back:
Before the patient leaves the operating room (Sign-out)

*   Ensures instrument/sponge counts are complete.
*   Confirms specimen labeling.
*   Reviews key concerns for recovery and management.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 70-year-old patient develops new-onset purulent sputum and a lung infiltrate 72 hours after being admitted for a hip fracture. What is the diagnosis and primary prevention strategy?
back:
Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP)

*   Prevention: Strict hand hygiene and elevation of the head of the bed.
*   Avoidance of unnecessary gastric acid suppression.
*   Regular oral care with chlorhexidine.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the role of filtration in the preparation of intravenous fluids compared to autoclaving.
back:
Removal of Pyrogens and Heat-Sensitive Pathogens

*   Preferred for thermolabile (heat-sensitive) components.
*   Pore size 0.22 μm retains all bacteria and spores.
*   Prevents febrile reactions caused by dead bacterial endotoxins.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast 'Endemic' versus 'Epidemic' hospital-acquired infections in a surgical ward.
back:
Prevalence and Pattern

*   Endemic: Constant presence of infections at a baseline level in the facility.
*   Epidemic: An unusual, significant increase above the baseline for a specific organism or site.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Name the most important single practice for preventing the transmission of infectious agents between patients in a hospital setting.
back:
Hand Hygiene

*   Includes washing with soap and water or alcohol-based rubs.
*   Must be performed before and after patient contact.
*   Crucial for preventing cross-contamination via healthcare workers.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: To ensure the destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores, the standard autoclaving procedure requires exposure to saturated steam at a temperature of [___] degrees Celsius at 15 psi for 15–20 minutes.
back:
● 121°C
● Essential for killing spores (e.g., Clostridium)
● Uses moist heat to denature proteins
● Standard for heat-stable surgical instruments

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A hospitalized patient develops profuse diarrhea confirmed as Clostridium difficile. Despite using gloves, the physician must perform a specific hand hygiene action because alcohol-based rubs are ineffective against this pathogen's spores. Identify the required action.
back:
● Hand washing with soap and water
● Physical friction removes resilient spores
● Alcohol cannot penetrate the spore coat
● Mandatory for all enteric-precautions cases

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which moist heat (autoclaving) achieves microbial death more efficiently than dry heat.
back:
● Denaturation of structural proteins
● Disruption of non-covalent (hydrogen) bonds
● Water facilitates protein coagulation at lower temperatures
● Effective against vegetative cells and spores

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the isolation requirements for a patient with active Pulmonary Tuberculosis versus a patient with Neisseria meningitidis infection.
back:
● Tuberculosis: Airborne precautions (N95 respirator, negative pressure room)
● Meningitis: Droplet precautions (Surgical mask, 3-6 feet distance)
● TB particles remain suspended; Meningitis drops fall quickly

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the primary safety protocol for handling used needles and sharps to minimize the risk of occupational blood-borne pathogen transmission.
back:
● Never recap used needles
● Immediate disposal in puncture-proof sharps containers
● Use of 'no-touch' techniques where possible
● Prevents Hepatitis B, C, and HIV exposure

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Chemical agents designed to destroy or inhibit the growth of pathogenic microorganisms specifically on the surface of living tissues (skin/mucous membranes) are classified as [___].
back:
● Antiseptics
● Examples: 70% Ethanol, Povidone-iodine, Chlorhexidine
● Less toxic than disinfectants used on inanimate objects
● Used prior to venipuncture or surgery

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 30-year-old male is admitted with a high fever and a distinctive 'honey-colored' crusted rash on his face. Specify the transmission-based precaution and the duration of isolation required.
back:
● Contact Precautions (Gown and Gloves)
● Diagnosis: Impetigo (S. aureus/S. pyogenes)
● Isolate until 24 hours of effective antibiotic therapy
● Prevents spread via direct touch or fomites

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Describe how Ethylene Oxide gas achieves sterilization for heat-sensitive items like endoscopes and plastic syringes.
back:
● Alkylation of proteins and nucleic acids
● Targets reactive hydrogen atoms on amino/hydroxyl groups
● Effective at low temperatures for plastics/electronics
● Requires post-sterilization aeration to remove toxic residue

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Differentiate between the concept of 'Standard Precautions' and 'Transmission-Based Precautions' in hospital-acquired infection (HAI) prevention.
back:
● Standard: Applied to ALL patients (blood, body fluids, non-intact skin)
● Transmission-Based: Added for specific suspected/confirmed pathogens
● Transmission types: Contact, Droplet, and Airborne
● Standard precautions assume every patient is potentially infectious

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: List the three mandatory checkpoints defined by the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist to ensure patient safety and prevent 'Never Events'.
back:
● Sign In: Before induction of anesthesia
● Time Out: Before skin incision
● Sign Out: Before patient leaves the operating room
● Confirms identity, site, procedure, and counts

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: To effectively clean hands when they are not visibly soiled in a clinical setting, the most appropriate agent to use is a/an [___]-based disinfectant.
back:
Alcohol-based hand rub.

*   Standard for routine hand hygiene.
*   Used when hands aren't visibly soiled.
*   Fast-acting and reduces bacterial counts efficiently.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 25-year-old patient is admitted with a high-grade fever, cough, and a maculopapular rash. Suspecting Measles, which specific isolation strategy must be implemented to prevent nosocomial spread?
back:
Airborne Precautions.

*   Required for small-particle aerosols.
*   Requires a private, negative-pressure room.
*   Healthcare workers must wear N95 respirators.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the role of the autoclave's pressurized steam mechanism in achieving the destruction of heat-resistant bacterial spores.
back:
Moist heat under pressure.

*   Achieves 121°C for 15-20 minutes.
*   Denatures and coagulates essential microbial proteins.
*   Kills highly resistant spores like Clostridium botulinum.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the personal protective equipment (PPE) and environmental controls required for Droplet Precautions versus Airborne Precautions.
back:
Droplet vs. Airborne:

*   Droplet: Surgical mask, no special ventilation, 3-foot distance.
*   Airborne: N95/FFP2 respirator, negative-pressure room, 6-12 air exchanges/hour.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the five clinical 'moments' for hand hygiene defined by the WHO to prevent the transmission of pathogens between patients.
back:
WHO Five Moments:

1. Before touching a patient.
2. Before a clean/aseptic procedure.
3. After body fluid exposure risk.
4. After touching a patient.
5. After touching patient surroundings.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The foundational practice of treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they are known to be infectious for HIV, HBV, and other bloodborne pathogens is called [___] precautions.
back:
Standard Precautions.

*   Applied to all patients regardless of diagnosis.
*   Includes hand hygiene and appropriate PPE.
*   Covers blood, secretions, and non-intact skin.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A surgical team is preparing for an appendectomy. Which specific action during the 'Time Out' phase of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist directly reduces the risk of post-operative surgical site infection?
back:
Antibiotic Prophylaxis Confirmation.

*   Verifies administration within the last 60 minutes.
*   Reduces bacterial load at the incision site.
*   Ensures therapeutic tissue levels during surgery.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Describe how 'Ring Immunization' functions as a specific isolation mechanism to control the spread of highly infectious diseases like Smallpox or Measles.
back:
Barrier of Immune Persons.

*   Vaccinates contacts and contacts-of-contacts.
*   Creates a 'buffer zone' of protected individuals.
*   Halts transmission by surrounding the infected reservoir.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish between the biological outcomes of sterilization and high-level disinfection regarding the survival of bacterial spores.
back:
Sterilization vs. Disinfection:

*   Sterilization: Complete destruction of all microbial life, including spores.
*   Disinfection: Eliminates most pathogens but does not reliably kill bacterial spores.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: List the appropriate isolation precaution for a patient diagnosed with Clostridium difficile or Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
back:
Contact Precautions.

*   Requires gloves and gown for all entries.
*   Dedicated patient-care equipment (e.g., stethoscopes).
*   Strict hand hygiene (soap and water for C. diff).

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The physical separation of infected individuals from others during the period of communicability to prevent the transmission of infectious agents to susceptible hosts is termed [___].
back:
Isolation.
- Protects the community from the reservoir.
- Duration depends on the period of communicability.
- Applied via standard, strict, or protective protocols.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 70-year-old patient admitted for a femur fracture develops a cough with purulent sputum 72 hours after admission. What is the most likely category of this infection?
back:
Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP).
- Presents >48 hours after hospital admission.
- Leading cause of healthcare-associated infection death.
- Predisposed by immobility and invasive devices.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the role of moisture and pressure in the mechanism of autoclaving for sterilizing surgical instruments.
back:
- Denatures microbial proteins and enzymes.
- Pressure allows steam to reach 121°C.
- Moisture facilitates the disruption of non-covalent bonds.
- Kills highly resistant spores within 15 minutes.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A patient with profound neutropenia is placed in a specialized hospital room. Contrast the goal of this room's isolation with that of 'Standard Isolation'.
back:
- Protective (Reverse) Isolation: Protects immunocompromised patients from external pathogens.
- Standard Isolation: Protects the community/staff from the infected patient.
- Uses HEPA filtration vs. source containment.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Outline the primary clinical strategy employed to prevent 'Never Events' such as retained surgical swabs in the operating theatre.
back:
WHO Surgical Safety Checklist.
- Obligatory sign-in, time-out, and sign-out.
- Verbally confirms instrument and sponge counts.
- Standardizes care to reduce human error.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The infection control practice of treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if they are known to be infectious for bloodborne pathogens is [___].
back:
Standard Precautions.
- Includes hand hygiene and PPE use.
- Involves safe handling of sharps.
- Applies to all patients regardless of diagnosis.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A nurse is preparing to insert an intravenous catheter. Which skin antiseptic should be prioritized to reduce the risk of contamination with skin flora like S. epidermidis?
back:
Iodine-containing compounds (Iodophors).
- More effective than 70% ethanol alone.
- Acts as an oxidizing agent.
- Inactivates essential sulfhydryl-containing enzymes.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Describe the mechanism by which 'Ring Immunization' controls the spread of a contagious disease during an active outbreak.
back:
- Vaccinates contacts of an infected individual.
- Creates a buffer of immune persons.
- Breaks the chain of transmission.
- Effectively encircles the reservoir to prevent spread.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish between the terms 'Quarantine' and 'Isolation' regarding the health status of the individuals involved.
back:
- Isolation: For persons known to be infected/ill.
- Quarantine: For healthy persons exposed to infection.
- Both limit movement to prevent transmission.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the biological indicator typically used to test the effectiveness of the autoclaving process in a hospital setting.
back:
Bacterial spores (e.g., Clostridium or Bacillus species).
- Most heat-resistant form of microbial life.
- Death of spores confirms sterilization.
- Requires 121°C at 15 psi.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: The primary practice implemented for all patients regardless of diagnosis to limit contact with blood, body fluids, and non-intact skin is known as [___] Precautions.
back: Standard Precautions. Includes hand hygiene, PPE (gloves, gowns, masks), and safe sharps handling. Assumes every patient is potentially infectious to break the chain of transmission.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A 30-year-old patient with chronic cough, night sweats, and apical cavitary lesions on chest X-ray is admitted. To prevent the spread of the infectious agent, the most appropriate isolation practice is [___].
back: Airborne Isolation. Requires negative-pressure rooms and N95 respirators for staff. Prevents transmission of small droplet nuclei (<5 microns) typical of pulmonary tuberculosis.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the efficacy and targets of Sterilization versus Disinfection in a hospital setting.
back: Sterilization kills all microorganisms including resistant bacterial spores (e.g., via Autoclaving). Disinfection reduces pathogens to safe levels but typically spares spores. Sterilization is mandatory for surgical instruments.

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: For the effective sterilization of surgical instruments, autoclaving must maintain steam at a temperature of 121°C under pressure for a minimum of [___] minutes.
back:
• 15 to 20 minutes
• Necessary to destroy highly resistant bacterial spores
• Operates at 15 lb/in² pressure

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A patient develops a purulent surgical site infection 72 hours after hospital admission. Identify the classification of this infection and the likely breach in care.
back:
• Nosocomial (Hospital-Acquired) Infection
• Onset occurs >48 hours after admission
• Often indicates a lapse in hand hygiene or aseptic technique

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which 70% ethanol acts as an antiseptic to prevent infection during venipuncture.
back:
• Disorganizes lipid structures in microbial membranes
• Denatures essential cellular proteins
• Requires water presence for maximal activity (70% vs 100%)

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Contrast the isolation durations required for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis versus a patient with chickenpox (varicella).
back:
• TB: Requires isolation until 3 weeks of effective chemotherapy
• Chickenpox: Isolation until all lesions have crusted (approx. 6 days)
• Both aim to prevent droplet or aerosol transmission

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Define the specific timeframe used to determine the duration of an absolute quarantine for a healthy individual exposed to a pathogen.
back:
• Matches the longest usual incubation period of the disease
• Restricts movement of healthy contacts to prevent spread
• Monitors for subclinical infectious states

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: To prevent the cross-transmission of pathogens, standard precautions require healthcare providers to perform hand hygiene [___] removing gloves.
back:
• Immediately after
• Prevents contamination from microscopic glove defects
• Follows WHO 'Clean Care is Safer Care' guidelines

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: A hospitalized patient is diagnosed with Hepatitis A. Which specific isolation practice is required to prevent the spread to other patients and staff?
back:
• Standard precautions with focus on enteric contact
• Isolation typically maintained for 3 weeks
• Strict hand-washing and proper disposal of excreta

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Describe the mechanism of 'ring immunization' as a patient-care practice to control the spread of highly contagious viruses like smallpox.
back:
• Vaccinating a 'ring' of contacts around an infected individual
• Creates a barrier of immune persons to halt transmission
• Prevents the pathogen from reaching new susceptible hosts

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Distinguish between the appropriate clinical use of disinfectants versus antiseptics in preventing the spread of infectious agents.
back:
• Disinfectants: Caustic chemicals for inanimate objects (e.g., floors, sinks)
• Antiseptics: Non-toxic chemicals for skin and mucous membranes
• Both reduce microbial load but differ in tissue toxicity

category: Discuss appropriate isolation and patient-care practices to prevent the spread of infectious agents
front: Identify the primary route through which the majority of hospital-acquired infections are spread between patients.
back:
• Direct contact via the hands of healthcare staff
• Can involve hospital dust or contaminated equipment
• Mitigated primarily through thorough hand-washing and barriers

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: The most important single procedure for preventing the horizontal transmission of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) among patients is [___].
back:
Handwashing (Hand Hygiene)
- Breaks the chain of infection between patients.
- Removes transient flora from healthcare workers' hands.
- Alcohol-based rubs are preferred unless hands are visibly soiled.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: A patient develops profuse, foul-smelling diarrhea after prolonged antibiotic use. To prevent environmental spread, staff must perform hand hygiene with [___] because alcohol-based rubs cannot kill spores.
back:
Soap and Water
- Clostridioides difficile spores are resistant to alcohol.
- Physical friction and rinsing are required for mechanical removal.
- Contact precautions must also include gown and glove use.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Explain how personal protective equipment (PPE) functions as a mechanism to interrupt the transmission of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
back:
Physical Barrier Mechanism:
- Gloves/gowns prevent direct contact with colonized skin.
- Protects healthcare worker clothing (fomites) from contamination.
- Disrupts transmission by limiting skin-to-skin contact between staff and patients.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Contrast the clinical application of Standard Precautions with Transmission-based Precautions.
back:
Standard vs. Transmission-based:
- Standard: Applied to all patients regardless of diagnosis (blood/body fluids).
- Transmission-based: Added for patients with highly transmissible pathogens.
- Categories include Contact, Droplet, and Airborne precautions.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Distinguish between disinfection and sterilization in terms of microbial efficacy.
back:
Sterilization vs. Disinfection:
- Sterilization: Destroys all microbial life, including resistant bacterial spores.
- Disinfection: Reduces pathogenic microorganisms but typically fails against spores.
- Sterilization requires autoclaving (121°C); disinfection uses chemicals like phenols.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: To prevent the suspension of Mycobacterium tuberculosis nuclei, patients must be placed in an 'Airborne Infection Isolation Room' featuring [___] pressure relative to the hallway.
back:
Negative Pressure
- Ensures air flows into the room, not out.
- Air is exhausted outdoors or through HEPA filters.
- Requires staff to wear N95 respirators for protection.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: A student presents with fever and neck stiffness. Until 24 hours of effective antibiotic therapy, staff must adhere to [___] precautions, requiring a surgical mask within 3 feet of the patient.
back:
Droplet Precautions
- Prevents transmission of Neisseria meningitidis or H. influenzae.
- Targets large respiratory particles that do not remain suspended.
- Requires private rooms or patient cohorting.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which moist heat in an autoclave kills heat-resistant bacterial spores.
back:
Protein Denaturation:
- Coagulates essential microbial proteins and enzymes.
- High pressure allows steam to exceed boiling temperatures.
- Water facilitates disruption of noncovalent bonds in protein structures.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Contrast the antimicrobial action and persistence of 70% Ethanol versus Chlorhexidine.
back:
Ethanol vs. Chlorhexidine:
- Ethanol: Rapidly denatures proteins/membranes; lacks residual activity.
- Chlorhexidine: Disrupts membranes and provides persistent, residual effect.
- Both are used for pre-surgical hand antisepsis.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Define the temporal criteria for a 'Nosocomial' or Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) following hospital admission.
back:
HAI Definition:
- Infection not present or incubating at admission.
- Manifests typically >48 hours post-admission.
- Includes infections acquired by staff or visitors within the facility.

category: Explain the importance of adherence to transmission-based precautions in reducing healthcare-associated infections
front: Infection control protocols mandate that [___] precautions be applied to all patients regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status to minimize risk from blood and body fluids.
back:
Standard Precautions.
• Includes hand hygiene and use of PPE (gloves, gowns, masks).
